tools.name: site_timeline_list_triggers
tools.description: List all available trigger types for animations. Returns 8 trigger types (pageLoad, scroll, hover, click, mouseMove, gesture, pageExit, cursor) with descriptions and examples. Call this to discover trigger options before using site_timeline_set_trigger.

tools.name: site_timeline_list_properties
tools.description: List all animatable CSS properties supported in from/to animation objects. Returns properties grouped by category (transform, appearance, dimensions, filter, background) with types and examples. Call this to discover what you can animate.

tools.name: site_timeline_list_easings
tools.description: List all available easing functions. Returns easing names grouped by category (power, sine, expo, circ, back, elastic, bounce) with descriptions. Also includes recommended easings for common use cases. Use 'power2.out' for subtle animations, 'power3.out' for punchy entrances.

tools.name: site_timeline_get_builder_state
tools.description: Get the current state of the animation builder. Returns the loaded timeline, its nodes, trigger configuration, and animation properties. Call this to orient yourself at the start of a session, or to check the current state after modifications. Returns guidance when no timeline is loaded.

tools.name: site_timeline_update_animation
tools.description: Update animation properties on an existing node. Accepts simplified from/to format (e.g., { opacity: 0, y: 50, x: '100px' }) with automatic unit handling. Duration, ease, stagger, split, and flap are top-level params. Returns the updated timeline state and generated code. Next: use site_timeline_preview_code to see the SDK output.

nodeUid.description: UID of the node to update

charset.description: Character set: 'alphanumeric', 'alpha', 'numeric', 'hex', 'binary', 'katakana', 'symbols', 'blocks', or a custom string

perspective.description: 3D perspective in pixels for flip type (default: 400)

styledBoard.description: Dark departure-board styling for board type (default: true)

stableWidth.description: Layout-shift strategy: false (off, default) | true/'cells' (pin each char cell to the widest glyph — classic split-flap look) | 'container' (pin only the parent's outer width, letters flow naturally inside — best for inline hover flappers)

preserveWhitespaceCells.description: Render whitespace as board tiles (default: false)

flap.description: Text flapper — split-flap display animation. Auto-enables split text (chars) if not set. Types: flip (3D rotate), fade, slide, blur, scale, board (departure board), none

tools.name: site_timeline_set_trigger
tools.description: Set the animation trigger type and options. Uses SDK trigger names: pageLoad, pageExit, scroll, hover, click, mouseMove, gesture, cursor. Each trigger type has specific options — call site_timeline_list_triggers first to see available options. Next: use site_timeline_add_animation or site_timeline_update_animation to configure the animation.

options.description: Trigger-specific options (e.g., { scrub: true } for scroll, { target: '.btn' } for click, { events: { onUp: 'play', onDown: 'reverse' }, animationStep: 0.05 } for gesture)

tools.name: site_timeline_set_property
tools.description: Set a single animation property with full store-level control. Use this for surgical edits when you need precise control over values and units (e.g., setting xUnit to 'vw' instead of the default '%'). For most cases, use site_timeline_update_animation instead.

tools.name: site_timeline_remove_property
tools.description: Remove a single animation property from a node. The property reverts to the element's natural CSS state. Use this to clean up unnecessary properties or reset specific values.

tools.name: site_timeline_preview_code
tools.description: Generate and preview the SDK code for the current timeline without saving. Returns the Motion.page SDK code that would be generated from the current animation state. Use this to verify your animation before committing changes.

tools.name: site_timeline_create
tools.description: Create a new animation timeline — the primary tool for starting a new animation. Accepts a name, trigger type (default: pageLoad), and optional initial animations with simplified from/to format. Creates everything atomically in one call. Next: use site_timeline_add_animation to add more elements, or site_timeline_preview_code to verify.

projectId.description: Project ID — use for website-based projects

artifactId.description: Artifact ID — use for standalone HTML/CSS/JS artifacts

pagePath.description: Page path within the project (e.g., '/', '/about', '/contact'). Defaults to '/'. Use site_navigate first to switch the webview.

isGlobal.description: Whether this timeline runs on all pages (default: false)

tools.name: site_timeline_add_animation
tools.description: Add an animated element to the current timeline — creates the node and sets its animation atomically, with no broken intermediate states. Accepts simplified from/to format with automatic unit handling. Default duration: 0.8s, default ease: power2.out. Next: use site_timeline_preview_code to verify, or site_timeline_add_animation again for more elements.

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element(s)

from.description: Starting animation properties (simplified: { opacity: 0, y: 50, x: '100px' })

charset.description: Character set: 'alphanumeric', 'alpha', 'numeric', 'hex', 'binary', 'katakana', 'symbols', 'blocks', or a custom string

perspective.description: 3D perspective in pixels for flip type (default: 400)

styledBoard.description: Dark departure-board styling for board type (default: true)

stableWidth.description: Layout-shift strategy: false (off, default) | true/'cells' (pin each char cell to the widest glyph — classic split-flap look) | 'container' (pin only the parent's outer width, letters flow naturally inside — best for inline hover flappers)

preserveWhitespaceCells.description: Render whitespace as board tiles (default: false)

flap.description: Text flapper — split-flap display animation. Auto-enables split text (chars) if not set. Types: flip (3D rotate), fade, slide, blur, scale, board (departure board), none

tools.name: site_timeline_list
tools.description: List all timelines in the current project or artifact. Returns timeline names, IDs, trigger types, and active status. Use this to discover existing animations before loading or editing. Returns guidance when no timelines exist. Next: use site_timeline_load to load one for editing.

tools.name: site_list
tools.description: List all projects in the connected Motion.page Desktop account. Returns project names, IDs, and URLs. Use this to discover available projects before filtering timelines by project, or to understand the project structure. Only available when connected to Motion.page Desktop.

tools.name: site_timeline_load
tools.description: Load a timeline into the builder for editing. Hydrates the store with the timeline's data — all subsequent mutations (site_timeline_update_animation, site_timeline_add_animation, site_timeline_set_trigger) operate on this timeline. Only one timeline can be loaded at a time. Next: use site_timeline_get_builder_state to inspect, or site_timeline_update_animation to modify.

tools.name: site_timeline_get
tools.description: Get read-only details of a timeline without loading it for editing. Returns metadata (name, trigger, active status) without hydrating the store. Use site_timeline_load instead if you want to edit the timeline.

tools.name: site_timeline_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a timeline. This action cannot be undone. If the deleted timeline is currently loaded, the store is reset. Use site_timeline_list first to verify the ID.

tools.name: site_timeline_rename
tools.description: Rename a timeline by ID. Changes only the display name — animations, trigger, and page assignment are untouched. Use site_timeline_list to find the ID.

name.description: New display name for the timeline

tools.name: site_timeline_set_active
tools.description: Toggle a timeline's active/inactive state. Inactive timelines are kept but do not run (and are excluded from page/project publishing). Use site_timeline_list to find the ID and see current status.

isActive.description: true to activate the timeline, false to deactivate it

tools.name: site_timeline_set_page_path
tools.description: Assign which page a timeline runs on, or mark it global (runs on every page). Provide `pagePath` for a specific page (e.g. '/', '/about'), or set `isGlobal: true` for site-wide. Use site_timeline_list to find the ID.

pagePath.description: Page path the timeline should run on (e.g. '/', '/about'). Omit when setting isGlobal.

isGlobal.description: true to run this timeline on all pages (global). When true, pagePath is ignored.

tools.name: site_timeline_publish
tools.description: Generate the full standalone bundle for the currently-loaded timeline. Returns wrapped, minified code plus the companion SDK bundle (`sdkBundle`) ready to ship. Unlike site_timeline_preview_code (which emits raw core code expecting the SDK to be loaded externally), this produces self-contained output. Use after site_timeline_create / site_timeline_load.

minify.description: Whether to minify the output (default: true)

tools.name: site_publish_page
tools.description: Bundle every active timeline attached to a given page into one standalone output. Requires a project context — if omitted, the active project and page path from the Desktop app are used. Global timelines are not included; use site_publish for site-wide output.

projectId.description: Project ID (optional — falls back to the active project)

pagePath.description: Page path (e.g., '/', '/about'). Falls back to the webview's current page.

minify.description: Whether to minify the output (default: true)

tools.name: site_publish
tools.description: Bundle every active timeline in a project (across all pages) into one consolidated standalone output. Returns wrapped, minified code plus the companion SDK bundle. If projectId is omitted, the active project from the Desktop app is used.

projectId.description: Project ID (optional — falls back to the active project)

minify.description: Whether to minify the output (default: true)

tools.name: artifact_publish
tools.description: Bundle every active timeline attached to a standalone artifact into one deployable output. Returns code + sdkBundle ready to inject into the artifact's JS. If artifactId is omitted, the currently-open artifact is used.

artifactId.description: Artifact ID (optional — falls back to the active artifact)

minify.description: Whether to minify the output (default: true)

tools.name: preview_inspect
tools.description: Inspect the DOM structure of the website loaded in the active tab. Returns semantic sections (hero, nav, footer…), a recursive node tree with CSS selectors, and element count. Use this to understand the page structure before creating animations.

tools.name: preview_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the current webview viewport (the live site page or artifact preview). Returns a PNG image. Use to visually verify page layout and animation targets before building animations. Distinct from canvas_screenshot, which captures the WebGPU canvas.

tools.name: preview_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the webview to a specific position. Accepts a pixel offset (top), a percentage (percent 0–100), or a CSS selector to scroll into view. Only one parameter is required.

top.description: Scroll to this absolute pixel position from the top of the page

percent.description: Scroll to this percentage (0–100) of the total page height

selector.description: CSS selector of an element to scroll into view

tools.name: preview_query
tools.description: Test a CSS selector against the page loaded in the active webview. Returns the matching element count and details (tag, classes, ID, bounding rect) for up to 50 elements. Use this to validate selectors before creating animations.

tools.name: preview_styles
tools.description: Get computed CSS styles for elements matching a selector in the active webview. Returns animation-relevant properties (opacity, transform, colors, dimensions, position, z-index, etc.) for up to 20 elements.

tools.name: preview_eval
tools.description: Execute arbitrary JavaScript in the active webview and return the result. The code runs inside an IIFE — use `return` to surface a value. Use this for runtime debugging, measuring scroll metrics, checking DOM state, or any inspection that the other tools don't cover.

code.description: JavaScript code to execute. Use `return` to get a value back. Example: `return { scrollHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight, scrollY: window.scrollY }`

tools.name: site_create
tools.description: Create a new project in Motion.page Desktop for a given website URL. Returns the created project with its ID. Use the returned ID with site_timeline_list or site_timeline_create.

tools.name: site_open
tools.description: Open an existing project in Motion.page Desktop. Switches to an existing tab for the project if already open, or opens a new tab and loads the project website in the webview.

projectId.description: Project ID to open (from site_list or site_create)

tools.name: site_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the webview to a specific page within the current project. Use this to switch between pages (e.g., from homepage to /about) before creating or editing animations for that page. The webview will load the page and wait for Motion.page SDK to initialize. Returns the new page URL.

tools.name: site_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a website project and all of its timelines. This action CANNOT be undone. If the project is open in a tab, the tab is closed. Use site_list first to verify the project ID.

tools.name: artifact_list
tools.description: List all artifacts in the connected Motion.page Desktop account. Artifacts are standalone HTML/CSS/JS creations (not tied to a website URL like projects). Returns lightweight metadata only — id, name, description, visibility, updatedAt. Does NOT include the HTML/CSS/JS source (that would be huge); call artifact_read with an id to get an artifact's source. Use this to discover existing artifacts before reading, editing, or creating timelines for them.

tools.name: artifact_read
tools.description: Read the current HTML, CSS, and JavaScript content of an artifact. Use this before making changes to see what's there — especially important if the user may have edited the artifact manually. Returns the full content of each file. Next: use artifact_patch for surgical edits, or artifact_update for full replacements.

tools.name: artifact_patch
tools.description: Apply surgical search-and-replace edits to an artifact's HTML, CSS, or JS without rewriting the entire file. Each patch targets a specific file ('html', 'css', or 'js') and replaces a search string with new content. Use artifact_read first to see the current content, then patch only what needs to change. This is much more efficient and less error-prone than artifact_update for small changes like fixing a color, adding a class, or tweaking a style.

search.description: Exact string to find in the file (must match exactly, including whitespace)

patches.description: Array of search-and-replace patches to apply

tools.name: artifact_create
tools.description: Create a new artifact in Motion.page Desktop. Artifacts are standalone HTML/CSS/JS creations — use them for self-contained animations, components, or experiments that don't require a website URL. Returns the created artifact with its ID. Next: use artifact_open to open it, then site_timeline_create to add animations.

tools.name: artifact_update
tools.description: Update an existing artifact's HTML, CSS, JS, or metadata. Use this to edit the artifact's code content. The artifact must exist — use artifact_list to find its ID first.

tools.name: artifact_open
tools.description: Open an existing artifact in Motion.page Desktop. Loads the artifact's HTML/CSS/JS in the editor and preview. If the artifact is already open in a tab, switches to that tab.

artifactId.description: Artifact ID to open (from artifact_list or artifact_create)

tools.name: artifact_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete an artifact and all its associated timelines. This action cannot be undone. Use artifact_list first to verify the ID.

tools.name: canvas_list_layer_types
tools.description: List every layer type available in the Canvas editor (90+ types), grouped by category: 'content' (2D shapes, 3D shapes ('shape-3d'), text, image, video, 3D models ('model-3d', GLB/GLTF), scene camera, lights, procedural shaders like metaballs/god-rays/mesh-gradient) and 'effect' (blur, glitch, halftone, water…). Returns {type, name, category, subcategory, description} per entry. Note: GROUPS are a third layer category but not a creatable type here — make them with canvas_create_group; they appear in canvas_get_state as category:'group'. Start here, then use canvas_get_layer_schema for the properties of specific types.

tools.name: canvas_get_layer_schema
tools.description: Get the full property schema for 1-5 canvas layer types: every property with its label, type, UI control, default, min/max/step, unit, and select options — plus transform defaults and the keyframable (animatable) property paths. Call this before canvas_add_layer or canvas_set_keyframes so values land in valid ranges.

tools.name: canvas_get_state
tools.description: Snapshot of the currently open canvas: settings, layer tree (id, name, type, category ('content' | 'effect' | 'group'), transform, blend mode, active layer mask, keyframe-track summary; group nodes carry their members in `children`), animation duration (latest keyframe time in seconds), timeline playhead state, selected layer, and save status. Pass detail:'full' for all property values, or layerId for one layer's complete state including raw keyframes. The `revision` field is `nonce:mutations` — a CHANGED NONCE between calls means the renderer reloaded and unsaved edits reverted to the last canvas_save; re-verify state before continuing.

detail.description: summary (default) keeps the response small; full includes every property value

layerId.description: Return complete state for this one layer

tools.name: canvas_list
tools.description: List the user's canvases (WebGPU shader/animation compositions): id, name, updatedAt, isPublic, published. Use canvas_open to start editing one.

tools.name: canvas_create
tools.description: Create a new canvas and open it in a tab. Optional settings: sizeMode ('stretch' fills the container, 'aspect' locks a ratio), aspectRatio (e.g. 1.7778 for 16:9, required for sizeMode 'aspect'), background (Fill object, e.g. {mode:'solid', color:'#000000'}), ambientLight (0-100), mouseTrackingScope ('window'|'canvas'). Edits are in-memory until canvas_save.

tools.name: canvas_open
tools.description: Open an existing canvas in a tab (or switch to it if already open). Subsequent canvas tools operate on this canvas.

tools.name: canvas_save
tools.description: Persist the open canvas (layers + settings) to the cloud, regenerate its bundle when eligible, and refresh the thumbnail. Canvas edits are in-memory (undo-able) until you call this.

tools.name: canvas_update_settings
tools.description: Patch the open canvas's settings: sizeMode ('stretch'|'aspect'), aspectRatio (number), background (Fill object e.g. {mode:'linear', angle:90, stops:[{color:'#ff0000', position:0},{color:'#0000ff', position:100}]}), ambientLight (0-100), mouseTrackingScope ('window'|'canvas'), markers (named timeline markers: [{time, label}]). Undo-tracked; unsaved until canvas_save.

markers.description: Named timeline markers ({time: seconds, label}); replaces the whole list

tools.name: canvas_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a canvas and its stored bundle/thumbnail. This cannot be undone — confirm with the user before calling. Closes the canvas's tab if open.

tools.name: canvas_add_layer
tools.description: Add a layer to the open canvas. Layer tree rules (enforced): CONTENT layers (shapes/media/shaders) live at the root or inside a group; EFFECT layers apply to everything below them at root, to one content layer when nested under it via parentId, or to a group's whole composite when nested under a group; GROUPS are containers made with canvas_create_group (not a layer type here) that accept content, effects, and nested groups. Properties are validated against the type's schema (use canvas_get_layer_schema first) and numeric values are clamped to their ranges. Returns the created layer with resolved values.

name.description: Display name (defaults to the type's name)

scale.description: Uniform scale factor (1 = natural size), around the layer center

rotateX.description: 3D rotation around the X axis in degrees

rotateY.description: 3D rotation around the Y axis in degrees

properties.description: Schema properties for this type (canvas_get_layer_schema shows valid names/ranges)

interactivity.description: Mouse tracking / cursor-warp settings (trackMouse, smoothing, cursorWarp, warpMode…)

parentId.description: Nest under this layer: a group accepts anything; a content layer accepts effects only (the effect then applies to that layer alone)

tools.name: canvas_update_layer
tools.description: Update an existing layer with a deep-partial patch. Patch keys: name, visible, locked, blendMode, transform (partial — x/y/width/height/rotation/scale/opacity/skewX/skewY/rotateX/rotateY/anchor/fit/mask-shape fields), properties (schema props, validated + clamped), interactivity, instancing, videoClip ({clipStart, clipEnd, timelineOffset, duration} — video layers only), mask ({sourceLayerId, channel: 'alpha'|'luma', invert} — use another CONTENT layer as an alpha/luma mask for this content layer, or to bound an effect's region; sourceLayerId: null disables). Returns the updated layer plus notes about any clamped values.

patch.description: Deep-partial patch; see description for valid keys

tools.name: canvas_remove_layer
tools.description: Remove one or more layers (children are removed with their parent). Undo-able in the editor.

tools.name: canvas_move_layer
tools.description: Move a layer in the tree: reorder among siblings (index) and/or re-parent (parentId; null moves it to the root). Nesting rules are enforced: groups accept anything (content, effects, nested groups); content layers accept effects only; effects accept no children; cycles are rejected. Layer order is paint order — later layers render on top.

parentId.description: New parent layer id, or null for root

tools.name: canvas_duplicate_layer
tools.description: Duplicate a layer (including nested effects and keyframes) with fresh ids, inserted right after the source.

tools.name: canvas_create_group
tools.description: Create a GROUP — an organizational container that composites its subtree into one unit, so its transform, opacity, blend mode, and any effect nested directly under it act on the whole group at once. Groups accept content layers, effect layers, and nested groups. Pass layerIds to move existing layers into the new group (in the given order); omit for an empty group. The group is inserted at the root, or inside another group via parentId. Animate the group's transform with canvas_set_keyframes to move/scale/fade all members together. Note: light layers inside groups are skipped by the renderer (v1 limitation).

layerIds.description: Existing layers to move into the group, in order

parentId.description: Nest the group inside this group (omit for root)

tools.name: canvas_set_keyframes
tools.description: Batch-upsert keyframes across layers and properties in ONE call — prefer this over many single edits. Each track is {layerId, path, keyframes:[{time (s), value, ease?}]}. Paths must be animatable for the layer type (canvas_get_layer_schema lists them): 'transform.x/y/width/height/rotation/scale/opacity/skewX/skewY/rotateX/rotateY' plus numeric schema props like 'metaballs.speed'. Groups animate too — keyframing a group's transform moves/scales its whole composite. Upserting at an existing keyframe's time updates its value/ease (that's also how you change an ease). Ease names are GSAP-style ('power1.inOut', 'expo.out', 'bounce.out' — see site_timeline_list_easings).

value.description: Raw value (clamped to the property's range)

tools.name: canvas_remove_keyframes
tools.description: Batch-remove keyframes. Each entry is {layerId, path, times?}: give times (seconds) to remove specific keyframes, omit times to delete the whole track.

tools.name: canvas_timeline_control
tools.description: Control the canvas keyframe timeline: play, pause, seek (to time in seconds), or set_loop (loop: true/false). Returns the current playhead state. Combine seek with canvas_screenshot's atTime to inspect specific moments.

tools.name: canvas_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the live WebGPU render of the open canvas as an image — your eyes on the canvas. Optionally pass atTime (seconds) to capture a specific timeline moment (the playhead is restored afterwards). Use after edits to verify the result visually.

atTime.description: Seek to this time (s) before capturing

tools.name: canvas_publish
tools.description: Publish the open canvas to the cloud: uploads any local media assets, regenerates the served embed bundle with cloud URLs, and marks the canvas published AND public (the embed endpoint only serves public canvases). Required before the embed link works and before canvas_export_bundle resolves media to cloud URLs. May take a while for large media.

tools.name: canvas_export_bundle
tools.description: Generate the standalone JS bundle + embed HTML snippet for the open canvas (same output as the editor's Publish modal). Returns {js, html, sizeBytes} — or, with saveToDesktop, the APP writes <name>.js + <name>-embed.html to the user's Desktop and returns their paths (no agent file access needed; the heavy js payload is omitted). If the canvas uses local media that hasn't been uploaded yet, this errors with guidance — run canvas_publish first so media resolves to cloud URLs.

saveToDesktop.description: Have the app write the bundle files to the user's Desktop and return their paths

tools.name: canvas_import_media
tools.description: Import a local media file (absolute path on this machine) into the open canvas's local asset store. Returns a localId (mp-local:…) to use as the `src` property of a video/image layer via canvas_add_layer, plus intrinsic width/height and durationSec for videos. No cloud upload — editing and canvas_export_video work from the local blob; only canvas_publish uploads.

path.description: Absolute path to the media file (.mp4/.webm/.mov/.png/.jpg/.webp/.gif)

tools.name: canvas_export_video
tools.description: Render the open canvas timeline to an MP4 using the native deterministic export engine. The APP writes the file (default: the user's Desktop when outputPath is omitted) — the agent needs no file access. Returns an exportId immediately (renders take minutes) — poll canvas_export_status until phase=done. The desktop app must stay open with the canvas tab visible for the whole render. One export at a time.

outputPath.description: Absolute output path ending in .mp4. OMIT IT to let the app save to the user's Desktop — the reply returns the resolved path. Agents never need filesystem access for exports.

range.description: Timeline range in seconds (default: 0 → timeline duration)

tools.name: canvas_export_status
tools.description: Poll a running canvas video export. phase: rendering → encoding → writing → done (or error / lost). `warnings` lists frames where video seeking was not frame-exact (seek timeout). When phase=done the MP4 exists at outputPath. phase=lost means the canvas renderer reloaded mid-export and the job died — re-run canvas_export_video.

tools.name: canvas_compose_capture
tools.description: Turn a screen-capture session (input-event log + footage geometry) into Screen-Studio-style camera zoom keyframes and smooth cursor motion on the open canvas. Computes deterministic zoom segments from click/type clusters, one clean cursor move per interaction, click timestamps for the cursor layer's ripple/warp, and beat markers. Applies directly to the given camera/cursor layers (removing their old transform tracks first); pass apply:false to get the manifest back instead. Typical flow: canvas_import_media the footage → add camera + cursor layers → this tool.

eventsPath.description: Absolute path to events.json — array of {t(ms), type:'move'|'click'|'type', x, y} and {type:'marker', kind:'beatStart'|'beatEnd', label} entries in page CSS pixels

events.description: Inline event log (small logs only — prefer eventsPath)

viewport.description: Capture viewport — the coordinate space of the event log

footage.description: Recorded footage geometry — used to reconcile dpr + window chrome

footageRect.description: Canvas-percent rect the footage occupies (top-left origin) — pass the device-mockup content rect for framed compositions; default full-bleed 0,0,100,100

zoom.description: Zoom policy overrides (defaults: level 1.5, dwell 1400ms, lead 450ms, pan-threshold 160px, max-gap 2500ms, zoom-out 0.8s)

smoothCursor.description: Anchor-based cursor motion, one eased move per interaction (default true)

cameraLayerId.description: Camera layer to receive transform.scale/x/y zoom tracks

cursorLayerId.description: Cursor layer to receive transform.x/y motion tracks + its clicks property

apply.description: Apply keyframes to the layers (default true when a layer id is given). false = return the full manifest for manual replay
